newsitem.title: EGYPT: Oman says taking part in Cairo Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: Oman says taking part in Cairo Mideast summit.

text.p: Oman said on Monday it would take part in a controversial Cairo Middle East economic conference scheduled for November which aims at integrating Israel into the regional economy.

"We will take part in the November economic summit but the level of representation has yet to be decided," Oman's ambassador to Egypt Abdullah bin Hamad bin Seif al-Bousaidi told reporters after talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
Unlike most Gulf Arab states who have boycotted the Jewish state, Oman and Israel share limited trade ties.

Lebanon has already said it would not attend the conference, which groups together more than 85 countries and several international organisations, saying it was premature and futile before there was complete peace in the region based on Israel's full withdrawal from occupied Arab lands.
Israeli troops occupy a strip in southern Lebanon. Beirut did not attend the two previous economic meetings which were held in Casablanca and Amman.
Israel also occupies Palestinian lands and the Syrian Golan Heights, captured in a 1967 war.
Mubarak also warned Israel that Arab participants at the conference might make difficulties for the Jewish state unless it made substantial progress in its peace negotiations.
He had threatened Israel in August with scrapping the summit but now Egyptian officials are trumpeting the event as a boon to the local and not regional economy.
